svg.title: Creating and sending an invoice exactly once
svg.desc: A sequence diagram with four lifelines: the user, the route handler, the store and PayPal. The route claims the request ID in the store with a hash of the body, creates a draft invoice at PayPal with the request ID in its memo, sends it, reads the invoice back and stores the result before answering the user. The lower half replays the same request ID: the store already holds a completed result, so the route returns it to the user and PayPal is not called.
svg.text: A repeated request ID returns the stored result and never calls PayPal.
Create invoice: draft and request ID
Recipient must be a sandbox buyer
Claim the request ID with the body hash
Create a draft, memo holds the request ID
The same request ID again: a double click or a retry
Same result. PayPal is not called.

g.text: The user creates an invoice. The form sends one request ID
The route checks the recipient before anything is claimed
The route claims the request ID in the store, before it calls PayPal
It creates a draft at PayPal. The draft ID is saved
Creating and sending are separate calls. Now it sends
It reads the invoice back, because PayPal's state is the truth
The result is stored with the request ID
The user sees the invoice, sent
A double click or a retry sends the same request ID again
The store already holds the finished result for that ID
The route returns that result. PayPal is not called a second time
